variant_decisions.evidence: ASV renders a transitive causative, "when I shall bring back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem", which is the hiphil qere ashiv (I will cause to return) with the captivity as its object. The ketiv ashuv is qal "I shall return", which the ASV wording does not carry. The lone note is classed alternative_rendering ("Or, return to"), so it bears only on English wording and does not decide the reading; the main-text wording does.

alignments.note: Initial conjunction left unrendered in ASV.

One 'al governs both coordinated nouns; the ASV distributes it as 'for ... and for', so both English prepositions are this morpheme's rendering (discontinuous unit). Reading the second 'for' as added is defensible but leaves a supplied word that a morpheme does license.

אֲשֶׁר ... שָׁמָּה is the relative-plus-resumptive-adverb idiom English fuses into the single word 'whither'. The corpus is 6-2 for one unit headed on the relative: 1KI.21.18 and 1KI.8.47 'whither', 1KI.17.19, 1KI.4.28 and 1KI.7.7 'where', 1KI.8.21 'wherein is' — and 1KI.8.47 and 1KI.21.18 fuse it across an intervening verb, so rule 35's distance clause covers this shape. 1KI.18.10 and 1KI.7.8 instead leave שָׁם unrepresented under rule 22, but rule 30's closing sentence puts rule 22 on a repetition of the same element rather than the parts of an idiom, and a relative plus a locative are not the same element. The directional he joins its host, as every Sd in the corpus does and as JOL.3.11's שָׁמָּה → 'thither' does here.

מִסָּבִיב is two units in the corpus, never one: 1KI.4.24 has the same phrase for the same 'round about' with מִן unrepresented, and 1KI.5.4 splits it with מִן taking 'on'. 'round about' carries only סָבִיב's own sense, so rule 30's fusion condition is unmet and rule 2 splits it. Matches JOL.3.11.
No article morpheme; the ASV's supplied *The* realizes the noun's own definiteness, so it joins the noun rather than being `added` (rules 15, 30).

'done to' is the ASV's rendering of the construct relation in חֲמַס בְּנֵי, so under rule 19 it belongs to the nomen rectum rather than being 'added'; splitting the supplied participle 'done' onto חֲמַס is defensible, but rule 19 leaves the first noun only its own English word.

Asyndetic relative clause: the supplied 'that' is licensed by the relative clause itself, whose only morpheme is this verb, so it joins the verb's unit rather than being 'added'. Attaching it instead to the antecedent 'blood' (s003) is defensible.
